name: poisson-validation
title: High-order accuracy verification: P1/P2/P3 optimal L2 convergence
question:
Do P1, P2, and P3 Lagrange elements each achieve their OWN theoretically
optimal L2 convergence rate (degree+1: 2, 3, 4 respectively) when solving
the dolfinx-backed `PoissonSolverStep` on a smooth (C-infinity)
manufactured solution, or does any element order under- or over-perform
its textbook rate?
hypothesis:
u_exact = sin(pi*x)*sin(pi*y) is smooth but NOT polynomial, so unlike a
quadratic manufactured solution (exactly representable by degree>=2
elements, collapsing their error to round-off) no fixed-degree Lagrange
space represents it exactly. Standard a priori FEM theory predicts every
degree-p Lagrange element converges in L2 at rate p+1 on a sufficiently
smooth problem: P1 -> O(h^2), P2 -> O(h^3), P3 -> O(h^4). A genuine
dolfinx solve, with the L2 error measured against the true symbolic exact
solution at elevated quadrature (not an FE interpolant of it, which would
understate exactly the higher-order error this check needs to see),
should reproduce all three optimal rates cleanly.
objective:
For degree in {1, 2, 3} and a resolution sweep (mesh cells per side: 8,
16, 32, 64), solve -div(grad(u)) = f on the unit square with f and the
Dirichlet BC derived from u_exact = sin(pi*x)*sin(pi*y), compute each
point's L2 error against the true exact solution, and fit the log-log
convergence rate (slope of log error vs log h) per degree. Confirm P1's
rate lands near 2.0, P2's near 3.0, and P3's near 4.0 -- a rigorous
multi-order verification, not a single "error is small" checkbox.
description:
Real dolfinx (0.11.0) throughout -- no faking. `PoissonSolverStep`
(`problem="smooth_trig"` config) solves the real spatially-varying-source
Poisson problem via `fem.solve_poisson` (interpolating both the source
f = 2*pi^2*sin(pi*x)*sin(pi*y) and the homogeneous Dirichlet BC as real
dolfinx `Function`s, NOT the constant-source shortcut the original
quadratic-MMS path uses). The L2 error is computed by
`fem.l2_error_exact`: it builds u_exact as a genuine symbolic UFL
expression via `ufl.SpatialCoordinate`/`ufl.sin`, and integrates
`(uh - u_exact)^2` at an ELEVATED quadrature degree (`2*(degree+3)`) --
deliberately NOT `fem.l2_error`'s approach of interpolating u_exact into
the same degree-p trial space as uh first, which would measure the
distance between two same-degree objects (partially masking the true
higher-order discretization error) rather than the true continuum L2
error P3's O(h^4) rate needs to be visible against.

The mesh uses dolfinx's "crossed" triangulation (`fem.build_mesh`'s prior
fix for the default uniform-diagonal mesh's P1 superconvergence
artifact on quadratic MMS problems). On THIS smooth-but-non-polynomial
solution, that artifact doesn't arise for any degree in the first place
(the Laplacian of sin(pi*x)*sin(pi*y) is not constant, so no fixed-degree
Lagrange space is exact for it) -- confirmed empirically below: all three
orders show clean optimal rates from the coarsest resolution (n=8)
onward, with no pre-asymptotic curvature to work around.

`high_order_verification` (this study's canonical baseline composite) is
a single (degree, resolution) point wired through the real
process-bigraph Composite/RAMEmitter machinery, run once (degree=2,
resolution=32) and cross-checked bit-for-bit against the direct sweep's
same point. The full P1/P2/P3 x resolution SWEEP that fits and verifies
each degree's rate lives in `sims/run.py` (same convention as
mesh-convergence's uniform-vs-adaptive sweep: the comparison/sweep logic
lives in the study, not the generator).

Achieved result (the committed production run): P1 -> finer-mesh-fit rate
1.998 (theory 2.0), P2 -> rate 3.000 (theory 3.0), P3 -> rate 4.000
(theory 4.0) -- all three within a hundredth of their theoretical optimal
L2 rate. Total wall-time for all 12 solves (3 degrees x 4 resolutions)
plus the baseline composite cross-check: ~2.7s.

expected_behavior.name: p1-achieves-optimal-rate
expected_behavior.en: P1 (degree=1) Lagrange elements achieve an L2 convergence rate within 0.25 of the theoretical optimum 2.0.
expected_behavior.rationale: Standard a priori theory: degree-1 Lagrange elements converge in L2 at O(h^2) on a sufficiently smooth problem. u_exact = sin(pi x)sin(pi y) is C-infinity, so P1 should hit this rate cleanly; achieved 1.998 (finer-mesh fit over resolutions 16/32/64).

expected_behavior.name: p2-achieves-optimal-rate
expected_behavior.en: P2 (degree=2) Lagrange elements achieve an L2 convergence rate within 0.25 of the theoretical optimum 3.0.
expected_behavior.rationale: Degree-2 Lagrange elements converge in L2 at O(h^3) on a smooth problem. Achieved 3.000 (finer-mesh fit over resolutions 16/32/64).

expected_behavior.name: p3-achieves-optimal-rate
expected_behavior.en: P3 (degree=3) Lagrange elements achieve an L2 convergence rate within 0.25 of the theoretical optimum 4.0.
expected_behavior.rationale: Degree-3 Lagrange elements converge in L2 at O(h^4) on a smooth problem -- the most demanding of the three orders to hit cleanly since it requires elevated quadrature to avoid becoming self-limited. Achieved 4.000 (finer-mesh fit over resolutions 16/32/64).

behavior_tests.name: p1-achieves-optimal-rate
behavior_tests.description:
P1's log-log L2-error-vs-h slope, fit over the finer half of the
resolution sweep (16/32/64, dropping the coarsest point to avoid any
pre-asymptotic contamination), must be within 0.25 of the theoretical
optimum 2.0.

provenance.note: A priori FEM theory: degree-p Lagrange elements converge in L2 at O(h^(p+1)) on a sufficiently smooth problem; p=1 -> rate 2.0. 0.25 is a generous margin around that theoretical value, not a fitted threshold; the achieved production rate is 1.998.

behavior_tests.name: p2-achieves-optimal-rate
behavior_tests.description:
P2's log-log L2-error-vs-h slope, fit over resolutions 16/32/64, must
be within 0.25 of the theoretical optimum 3.0.

provenance.note: p=2 -> theoretical L2 rate 3.0. 0.25 margin around theory; achieved production rate is 3.000.

behavior_tests.name: p3-achieves-optimal-rate
behavior_tests.description:
P3's log-log L2-error-vs-h slope, fit over resolutions 16/32/64, must
be within 0.25 of the theoretical optimum 4.0.

provenance.note: p=3 -> theoretical L2 rate 4.0, the most demanding of the three orders (requires elevated quadrature so the check isn't itself quadrature-limited -- see fem.l2_error_exact). 0.25 margin around theory; achieved production rate is 4.000.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
All three element orders (P1/P2/P3) achieve their theoretically optimal
L2 convergence rate within tolerance, confirming the dolfinx bridge is
not just correct at one order (the original quadratic-MMS check) but
genuinely high-order-accurate across P1-P3, before building the
convergence sweep and time-stepped diffusion studies on top of it.

canonical_runs.label: High-order verification: P1/P2/P3 vs sin(πx)sin(πy), resolutions 8/16/32/64

embed_visualizations.name: convergence-multi-order
embed_visualizations.description: Log-log L2 error vs mesh size for P1/P2/P3, each with a fitted rate and a dotted theoretical-optimal-rate reference triangle.

embed_visualizations.name: solution-heatmap
embed_visualizations.description: Interactive Plotly heatmap of the smooth manufactured solution u = sin(πx)sin(πy).

conclusion:
All three element orders hit their theoretically optimal L2 convergence
rate: P1 -> 1.998 (theory 2.0), P2 -> 3.000 (theory 3.0), P3 -> 4.000
(theory 4.0), fit over the finer half of an 8/16/32/64 resolution sweep.
The dolfinx bridge is confirmed genuinely high-order-accurate, not merely
correct at a single order -- the pipeline gate for mesh-convergence and
transient-diffusion.
